$comment: Member kinds this lexicon supplies to a chant workspace (#3932). chant reads this file as data and never imports the lexicon. A dbt project reads the tables a sql member declares, so its kind ships beside them. Its reader, dbt-project, is chant's own code: it parses dbt_project.yml and the sources YAML under the model paths, never runs dbt, never renders Jinja and never reads profiles.yml, and turns each source table and column into a link to the sql member's <schema>.<table> and <schema>.<table>.<column> outputs (#3931). The same pass exposes each model as an output, <schema>.<model> and <schema>.<model>.<column> where the model's YAML lists columns (#3935); the schema is the modelSchema field, or the custom schema dbt config names when the project's generate_schema_name makes that independent of the target.

kinds.name: dbt
kinds.description: a dbt project, with a dbt_project.yml in its directory; its sources link to the tables and columns a sql member declares, its models are outputs other members link to, and dbt is never run

sqlMember.description: The member whose tables the project's sources read. Unset, each source table links to the one member that exposes it, and a table two members expose is ambiguous (WSP095).

dialect.description: How source names are cased before they are matched: postgres folds an unquoted name to lowercase and keeps a quoted one as written, the way dbt-postgres quotes a source's schema and identifier unless quoting turns it off; clickhouse keeps every name as written.

modelSchema.description: The schema the project's models land in. When set, each model is the output <modelSchema>.<model> and dbt's config is not read for the schema. Unset, chant reads +schema, the model YAML's config and the model's config(schema=...), and a model whose schema depends on the target (dbt's default generate_schema_name joins the target schema to a custom one) is reported as a gap (WSP099) that asks you to set this field.
